newsitem.title: USA: Fed Vice Chair Rivlin says U.S. economy doing fine.
newsitem.headline: Fed Vice Chair Rivlin says U.S. economy doing fine.

text.p: Federal Reserve Vice Chair Alice Rivlin said on Tuesday that the U.S. economy has produced as good a set of economic statistics in memory, perhaps ever.
"The American economy is doing fine," she told a credit union group, adding: "it is as good a set of economic statistics at the aggregate level as American economists have seen, perhaps ever."
She said that on balance, despite some pockets of joblessness, "we do not have at the moment whole regions falling behind as we did in the 1970s and 1980s."
Rivlin also lauded tight labor markets, saying they allowed those at the bottom end of the economy to get jobs and get work experience.
"Tight labor markets are basically a very good thing, not just for those looking for jobs now, but for the future health and productivity of our economy," she said.
She added that "these tight labor markets mean that poeple are getting job experience who might have been unemployed or on welfare."
But she said the biggest threat to the current excellent economic environment would actually be "too much of good thing, an overheated economic followed by inflation, a boom followed by a bust."
She said it was the Fed's job to keep a watchful eye for imbalances and signs of overheating. "to be ever vigilant that too much of a good thing takes over"
But she said economists, including those at the Fed, have been surprised and gratified so far by the lack of signs of imbalance and overheating.
She said that she was also gratified by price behavior, noting that businesses so far have been able to absorb wage increases without raising prices and profits have been holding up well.

"We can't be sure how long that will last, it's not likely that the ups and downs of the economy which we have known forever have suddenly gone away, so the Federal Reserve is watching carefully, especially the price indices," she said.
